file_insights.key_content: Complete Cascading Discount System Plan with 11 sections: Executive Summary, Current Discount Landscape, Cascading Formula Definition with worked examples, Cascading vs Additive comparison, New field requirements, UI layout plan, JS real-time calculation, Python server-side validation, Affected DocTypes matrix, Integration with existing calculate_totals(), Acceptance criteria
file_insights.significance: Comprehensive specification document replacing single-tier discount model with 3-tier cascading formula: final_price = base_price * (1 - d1/100) * (1 - d2/100) * (1 - d3/100)

changes: Updated subtask-3-1 notes with comprehensive scan results of 120+ parent DocTypes
Updated subtask-3-2 status to in_progress with 124.md generation note

patterns_discovered.formula: Percentage: unit_price * discount_value / 100; Fixed: min(discount_value, unit_price)
patterns_discovered.implementation: cart_line.py lines 104-125 with flt() precision throughout

patterns_discovered.limitation: Does not cascade; sums independent discount sources

patterns_discovered.principle: Server-side Python is single source of truth

patterns_discovered.scope: All numeric discount operations across 7 apps

gotchas_discovered.description: Three sequential discounts compound multiplicatively, not additively. Combined discount can never exceed 100% but calculation is more complex than simple percentage addition.
gotchas_discovered.example: 10% + 10% + 10% cascading ≠ 30% additive; actual result is 72.9% off (0.9 * 0.9 * 0.9 = 0.729)

gotchas_discovered.description: If discount_1 = 100%, subsequent discounts become meaningless (price already zero). Must validate total cascaded discount never exceeds 100% effective reduction.
gotchas_discovered.validation_needed: Reject d1=100 if d2 or d3 are non-zero

gotchas_discovered.description: Current code does not explicitly validate against negative discount values. Negative discounts represent price increases and may have business meaning but require clear intent.
gotchas_discovered.codebase_gap: No existing validation in cart_line.py or order.py

gotchas_discovered.description: Existing discount_percentage field used across 11 DocTypes must be repurposed as discount_1 without breaking current orders/quotations.
gotchas_discovered.migration_required: Data migration script needed to map existing discount_percentage → discount_1

gotchas_discovered.description: Coupon supports 4 discount types (Percentage, Fixed Amount, Free Shipping, Buy X Get Y) with separate max_discount_amount cap. Not compatible with pure cascading formula.
gotchas_discovered.scope_impact: Coupon integration requires special handling outside 3-tier cascade

gotchas_discovered.issue: Listing vs Order Discount Models Divergence
gotchas_discovered.description: Listing uses price-level discounting with compare_at_price, selling_price, wholesale_price. Order uses percentage-based. These models conflict in a unified cascading system.
gotchas_discovered.design_decision_needed: Whether Listing discounts follow cascading or remain price-level

gotchas_discovered.description: Computing discount_1_amount, discount_2_amount, discount_3_amount separately requires careful rounding at each step to avoid cumulative floating-point errors.
gotchas_discovered.mitigation: Must use flt(value, 2) at every intermediate calculation

gotchas_discovered.description: Showing/hiding Discount 2 and 3 tiers via toggle buttons requires JS event handler coordination to ensure intermediate amounts recalculate when tiers become visible.
gotchas_discovered.js_risk: Race conditions if discount fields change while tiers are hidden

approach_outcome.business_alignment: Justified 3-tier cascading model as correct B2B representation vs additive; explains why each discount applies to already-reduced price
approach_outcome.integration_points_documented: Existing calculate_totals() dual-layer pattern extended; backward compatibility path provided; all 11 affected DocTypes enumerated

recommendations.rationale: Existing discount_percentage fields across 11 DocTypes must map to discount_1 without data loss. Critical for backward compatibility.
recommendations.action: Design and test data migration for Order, Quotation, Cart Line, Sub Order Item, etc.

recommendations.recommendation: Implement comprehensive edge case test suite first
recommendations.rationale: Floating-point precision with cascading formula is error-prone. Must test 0%, 100%, negative, and boundary cases.
test_cases: d1=50%, d2=50%, d3=50% (should give 87.5% total, not 150%)

recommendations.rationale: Not all 11 DocTypes are equally complex. Start with Order/Quotation (simplest), then Cart Line items, then tackle Coupon (most complex)
phases: Phase 2: Cart Line, Sub Order Item, Marketplace Order Item

recommendations.recommendation: Document user-facing messaging about cascading behavior
recommendations.rationale: Business users may not understand that 10% + 10% ≠ 20% off. Clear messaging prevents support escalations.
recommendations.content: Tooltip or help text explaining cascading formula with simple example (e.g., 'Each discount applies to the price after the previous discount')

recommendations.rationale: Current plan documents Listing tier-based pricing separately. Must decide: does Listing follow 3-tier cascade or remain price-level?
recommendations.decision_needed: Architecture review required for Listing, Listing Bulk Pricing Tier, Product Pricing Tier consistency

recommendations.rationale: Coupon's 4 discount types (Percentage, Fixed, Free Shipping, BOGO) with max_discount_amount cap don't fit the 3-tier cascade model cleanly.
recommendations.action: Separate design document for how Coupon interacts with cascading discounts on Cart/Order

recommendations.recommendation: Add performance considerations to implementation plan
recommendations.rationale: Cascading formula with 3 tiers requires more JS recalculation than current single-discount. Assess impact on form render time with large cart line counts.
recommendations.metric: Benchmark calculate_totals() performance with 100+ line items before/after cascading

recommendations.rationale: Current plan hardcodes 3 tiers. If business later wants 4 or 5 tiers, architecture should support it.
recommendations.future_design: Use array-based tier structure vs hardcoded discount_1, discount_2, discount_3 fields
